status: scene definition; every dimension is a design value chosen for the simulation, not a measurement of real hardware. Connector dimensions follow the nominal TIS 166-2549 / CEE 7/16 / NEMA values in connector/catalog.py

connector.description: Catalog connector: Thai 3-round-pin plug (Type O) in a universal Thai socket with keyhole line/neutral openings and a round earth hole (connector/catalog.py); plug-dependent numbers below (socket x, plug_spawn z, cable attach) are checked against the spec by envs/workspace.validate

frames.description: World origin is the OpenArm v1 base (openarm_body_link0). +X points across the table away from the robot, +Y along the table, +Z up. The table top is 0.32 m above the robot base so every plug/socket/waypoint coordinate from earlier task configs stays valid.

pedestal.description: Column under the robot base, floor to the underside of the upstream base meshes

socket.note: x = fixture front face (0.4685) - socket depth 0.023; 6.4 mm further from the robot than v1 so the home pose leaves the 21.4 mm earth pin clear of the entry (pre-insert distance 27.4 mm); z lowered 6 mm because the Type O grasp frame sits 6 mm above its mating frame

plug_spawn.note: z = table top 0.32 + housing bottom offset (half height 0.010 - centre 0.006) + 2 mm settle drop

appliance.description: Box the cable is fixed to, standing on the floor under the table; the cable anchor is on its -X face

cable.mass_note: Light 2-core cord: with 0.75 m hanging to the floor a 0.07 kg/m cable pulled the 45 g plug across the table (0.5 N vs ~0.2 N table friction); at 0.035 kg/m the edge friction leaves ~0.1 N on the plug
cable.layout_note: Same route as workspace_v2 with 30 segments (5 cm each) instead of 60: along the table to the robot-side edge, 16 segments = 0.80 m down the 0.75 m drop, the rest coils on the floor. Halving the segment count cuts physics wall time ~3.8x (70.9 -> 18.7 s per simulated s, measured); per-joint bend stiffness unchanged, so the cable is effectively stiffer.

socket_leaves.description: One spring leaf per socket opening the plug uses: round pins are pressed from the outer wall toward the socket centre (line/neutral along -/+Y, earth along -Z), blades in a keyhole outward from the inner web; insertion resistance = n_leaves * friction * normal force
socket_leaves.push_force_note: Scripted insertion stops advancing its position target while the measured axial socket force exceeds this cap (force-limited push); it bounds the wind-up of the compliant arm and the face impact at seating
socket_leaves.wall_force_note: With spring retention the socket walls guide the pins and the housing face bottoms out on the socket face plate under the leftover push force, so the rigid-socket 5-8 N wall abort would reject every successful seating; the 0.2 mm penetration limit is unchanged

gripper_pads.description: Flat rubber pad plate on each right finger, 0.1 mm proud of the upstream mesh face so the pinch is a box-box contact patch (the mesh gave one contact point per finger, which cannot resist pitch about the pinch line)

scene_rgb.description: Right-side raised mount (moved 2026-10 for requirement 1: the plug must be seen from reset through closure). 0.48 m over the table top and 0.26 m outside its right edge, aimed at (0.29, -0.365, 0.376), 50 deg from vertical, level (no roll). Previous pose, for traceability: position (0.12, -0.21, 0.98), xyaxes (0, -1, 0, 0.9114, 0, 0.4116), fovy 48, aimed at (0.40, -0.21, 0.36) from above and behind the right hand. Measured on the 30 recorded recovery episodes (pickup frames incl. 5 random +-0.05 rad right-arm start postures per episode, per-episode camera jitter, per-episode socket placement): plug seen by overhead or wrist in 100 percent of pickup frames versus 89 percent with the previous pose (overhead alone 89 percent, wrist alone 68 percent); socket seen by this camera in transit_place/approach/align/insert/hold/withdraw 1.00/1.00/1.00/0.96/0.40/1.00 versus 0.46/0.11/0.19/0.03/0.00/0.00 with the previous pose. See docs/WORKSPACE.md.

depth.description: Overhead depth stream (obs depth/scene, 240x320 aligned to scene_rgb), modelled as a D435 exactly like the chest camera: rendered z-depth degraded with Intel's RMS noise, range limits, edge holes and dropout, 1 mm units
depth.depth_fx_note: focal length of the D435 depth imagers at 848x480 (87 deg HFOV): 424 / tan(43.5 deg)

chest_rgbd.description: workspace_v2_cable30_stockchest (2026-10-31, branch testing, preview): the real OpenArm v1 stock chest mount. The D435_camera_mount_v2 bracket (openarm_hardware 1.1.0, Attachments/chest-camera_D435) bolts with two M6 T-nuts 30 mm apart into the front face of the 60x60 column (front face x 0.03) and holds the D435 straight ahead, tilted 45 deg down; the angle is inferred from the bracket hole pattern (D435 rear M3 pair and M6 pair, axes 45 deg apart), not from an assembly drawing, which does not place the camera. Height 0.50 m chosen by the user (the bracket slides along the column); optical centre estimated 5 cm in front of the column face. Measured on the 2 episodes of data/cams_preview_real (same scenes and motion as data/cams_preview): plug seen transit_pick/descend/close/lift 0.48/0.34/0.31/0.27, socket 0.00 in transit_place/approach/align/insert. The rest of the file equals workspace_v2_cable30_cams.json. data/cams_preview_real was recorded with this file before this description was written; that exact file is data/cams_preview_real/workspace_used.json.

depth.description: Rendered z-depth (aligned to RGB) degraded like a D435 z16 stream: RMS noise z^2*subpixel/(fx*baseline) (Intel), 0 outside [min, max] range, holes at depth jumps, random dropout, 1 mm units
depth.depth_fx_note: focal length of the D435 depth imagers at 848x480 (87 deg HFOV): 424 / tan(43.5 deg)

visual_mount.description: D435 module 90 x 25 x 25 mm behind the optical centre; visual only, no mass, no collision

depth.description: Wrist depth stream (obs depth/wrist, 240x320 aligned to wrist_rgb), modelled as a RealSense D405: a short-range stereo module (ideal range 7-50 cm) whose depth comes from the same imager as its RGB, so it is aligned. Rendered z-depth degraded with Intel's RMS noise (short baseline, finer subpixel error), 0 below 7 cm / above 1 m, edge holes, dropout, 1 mm units. The D405 has NO IR projector, so untextured surfaces would give more holes on real hardware; this is not modelled. The action-camera visual housing below is kept unchanged so the RGB pixels do not change.
depth.depth_fx_note: assumed 87 deg HFOV at 848x480, like the D435: 424 / tan(43.5 deg)

visual_mount.description: Action-camera style housing behind the optical centre; visual only, no mass, no collision
